<reflection>
The third experiment introduced initial product (P=0.2) with substrate S=1.0 and catalyst cat=0.01. The fitting results show that M16 remains the best fit, followed closely by M14, M20, and M11. M9 is also plausible but with a higher negative log-likelihood. Many other mechanisms have similar NLL values, indicating that while product addition provided some discrimination, substantial uncertainty remains over the entire set. My aim to test for reversibility and product-induced effects was achieved, as mechanisms like M17 and M12 (which involve product interactions) showed relatively worse fits, but further differentiation is needed.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
By increasing the substrate concentration to 2.0 M while keeping catalyst at 0.01 M and no initial product, we probe the substrate dependence of the reaction kinetics. This experiment will help distinguish mechanisms with substrate inhibition or substrate-dependent inactivation (e.g., M11: S+cat=>inactive_catS, M16: S+catS=>inactive_catS2) from those without. At high substrate, such inactivation pathways should lead to pronounced deceleration in product formation over time, whereas mechanisms without substrate-induced inactivation may show standard saturation kinetics. Additionally, mechanisms with dimerization or catalyst-catalyst interactions (e.g., M2, M3, M19) may exhibit different scaling with substrate concentration. This design is effective because it introduces a new variable (substrate concentration) that differentially affects a broad range of candidate mechanisms, avoiding extreme conditions that might collapse mechanistic differences (e.g., full saturation or depletion) and building on previous experiments by complementing the variations in catalyst and product.
</hypothesis>
